descriptionChirho: Cud, the regurgitated food that ruminant animals chew; used exclusively in Levitical dietary legislation (Lev 11, Deut 14) to distinguish clean from unclean animals. English 'cud/the cud', Spanish 'bolo/rumia', Hindi जुगाली, Arabic جِرَّةً/جِرَّةٍ, Korean 새김질, Swahili 'mcheo/cheuo'. The conjunctive form (and-cud) is a grammatical variant with no semantic distinction from the standalone noun.
